status.label: In the normal range
status.explanation: Your HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over roughly the last 2–3 months and is below the 5.7% threshold used for prediabetes.

summary: Your HbA1c of 5.4 is in the normal range, which is a great sign for your long-term health. Your BMI of 17.6 falls into the underweight category, so a key focus area for you is building up healthy weight through balanced nutrition. Following your calorie target of 1700 calories a day, staying lightly active, and keeping up with routine checks like HbA1c and blood pressure monitoring will help you stay on track. Since you don't have other risk factors right now, this is a good time to build strong habits for the future.

foods_to_eat: Whole grains like brown rice, whole wheat, and millets
Pulses and legumes such as rajma, chana, and moong dal
Paneer, milk, and curd for protein and healthy weight gain
Nuts and seeds like almonds, walnuts, and peanuts
Healthy fats such as ghee and cold-pressed oils in moderate amounts
foods_to_avoid: Deep-fried snacks like samosas and pakoras
Refined flour products like maida-based bread and biscuits
Processed and packaged snacks high in salt or sugar
plan.portion_guidance: Since your BMI is in the underweight range, focus on slightly larger portions and include energy-dense but healthy foods like nuts, ghee, and dairy. Eat at regular intervals, including the suggested snacks, to meet your calorie target of 1,700 kcal without skipping meals.
plan.hydration: Drink about 8 to 10 glasses of water through the day. You can include a glass of milk or buttermilk with meals for extra nourishment, and limit tea or coffee to twice a day.
based_on: underweight BMI: higher energy density foods

exercise: Start with 15-20 minutes of gentle moderate activity like brisk walking or cycling, 3 days a week, and build gradually toward about 150 minutes a week as your fitness allows.

Add light strength training (bodyweight exercises, resistance bands, or light weights) on 2 non-consecutive days a week to help build muscle, which is especially helpful since you're in the underweight category.
Include a few minutes of stretching or mobility work after each session to support flexibility and recovery.
lifestyle.walking_goal: Begin with a 15-minute walk most days, aiming for 4-5 days a week, and gradually build up to 30 minutes a day, 5-6 days a week as it feels comfortable.
lifestyle.weight_management: Your BMI falls in the underweight range, so the focus should be on nourishing your body well rather than losing weight. Try to eat regular, balanced meals and snacks that include enough protein, healthy fats, and whole grains, and consider speaking with a dietitian for personalised guidance on gradually building a healthy weight.
lifestyle.sleep: Aim for 7-9 hours of sleep each night. Try to keep a consistent sleep and wake time, limit screens for about an hour before bed, and create a cool, dark, quiet sleeping space to help you wind down.
stress: Practice deep breathing exercises, such as inhaling for 4 counts and exhaling for 6 counts, for a few minutes each day.
Try mindfulness or meditation apps for 5-10 minutes daily to help calm your mind.
Consider journaling your thoughts or practicing gentle yoga to release tension and support emotional balance.
behaviour_change: Keep building consistent, gentle activity habits and celebrate small wins to stay motivated.
Since you don't currently smoke or drink, keep up these healthy choices as they support your overall well-being.
Focus on building a positive relationship with food, emphasizing nourishment and energy over restriction.

monitoring.name: HbA1c
monitoring.why: Regular screening finds changes before symptoms appear.
monitoring.frequency: Every 3 years, or yearly if your doctor advises because of risk factors

monitoring.name: Blood pressure
monitoring.why: High blood pressure multiplies the heart and kidney risks of high blood glucose.
monitoring.frequency: At every doctor visit; at home regularly if you have high blood pressure

preventive_actions: Aim to consistently meet your daily calorie target of 1700 calories using nutrient-dense vegetarian foods
Include protein-rich foods like lentils, dairy, and legumes to support healthy weight gain
Keep track of your blood pressure and HbA1c at routine checkups, even though both are currently normal
Build in light physical activity most days, such as walking or yoga, to support overall wellness
Pay attention to any unplanned weight loss or appetite changes and mention them to your doctor

hba1c_caveat: HbA1c can be less accurate if you have anaemia, kidney disease, a recent blood transfusion or certain haemoglobin variants.
